nodes.question: What multi-stakeholder initiative is mentioned as being institutionalized through the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
nodes.answer: SDG 17 on Partnerships for the Goals is the multi-stakeholder initiative mentioned.

This view gained the support of some UN agencies (UNEP, FAO, UNDP 2023), and was further institutionalised through the UN Global Compact, and in the UN Sustainable Develop- ment Goals (SDGs) through SDG 17 on Partnerships for the Goals (United Nations 2015). The multi-stakeholder approach was also promoted by powerful business associa- tions, most prominently the World Economic Forum (WEF) through its Global Redesign Initiative, reflecting a broader vision of stakeholder capitalism (Canfield et al. 2021). According to this vision, the WEF through its chairman Klaus Schwab believe that private corporations as stake- holders should play the leading role in sustainable devel- opment (Schwab and Vanham 2021) and be positioned as trustees of society in response to today S social and envi- ronmental challenges (Schwab 2019). These developments have had several major implications for GFG. For example, it has resulted in the proliferation of prominent multi-stakeholder initiatives, partnerships, 179 The rise of multi stakeholderism, the power of ultra processed food corporations, and the platforms, and roundtables involving the world S largest transnational food corporations, their affiliated business interest groups, along with multilateral agencies, interna- tional non-governmental organizations, national govern- ments, and research institutions.

nodes.question: What role does a place-based approach play in sustainability efforts?
nodes.answer: A place-based approach can assist with scaling-up local innovation or scaling-down larger sustainability agendas like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to an implementable level.
nodes.paragraph: These changes, viewed with a more-than-human (Sensu Seymour and Con- nelly 2023) lens, can prevent exclusion of externalities com- mon with many reductionist and mechanistic approaches to sustainability; this lens acknowledges the rights of the non- human and reflects the values of multispecies justice (Sensu Tschakert et al. 2021). Introduction It is imperative that agricultural production systems move swiftly towards improved ecological-based and sustainable models of agriculture (agroecological transition) that pro- duce food, fibre, and fuel within the planetary boundaries. These changes need also to acknowledge human health, and equity issues (Abdourahamane Illiassou and Oeba 2020). There is a call for place-based solutions which are increas- ingly identified as an approach to addressing contextual nuance while remaining relevant to wider policy agendas. This need for simultaneous local and global relevance has also been referred to as glocal (Demblans et al. 2020). nodes.question: How can local authorities enhance their efforts in promoting urban sustainability based on the information in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Local authorities can enhance their efforts by collaborating with national, regional, or global networks and initiatives to address environmental vulnerability in urban areas.
nodes.paragraph: This consolidated framework for assessing and integrating multiple environmental pressures is a vital tool for urban strategic planning. It addresses the complex interplay of urban factors, offering a proactive, transparent, and cost-effective approach to mitigate environmental pressures and promote sustainable urban development amidst the ongoing climate crisis. The methodology's replicability under - scores its potential for broad application, contributing to the global effort in achieving urban sustainability and resilience. Keywords Air quality Urban heat Green space Adaptation Mitigation Urban resilience Introduction Urban sprawl, along with the accompanied implications (e.g., pollution, urban heat stress, biodiversity loss), is one of the biggest challenges that modern societies are confronted with (Humbal et al. 2023). Today, the degree of urbanization globally is close to 57%, while among continents Europe has the third highest level of urbanization with three quarters of the population residing in urban areas ( Urbanization by continent 2022, n.d., Stanners and Bourdeau 1995), also indicating the degree of environmental vulnerability that cit- ies are exposed to. nodes.question: What was the key reason cited by the project coordinator of Euro cities for the success of Sumps in integrating sustainability into mobility plans?
nodes.answer: The project coordinator mentioned that Sumps set an example for smaller cities around those that have implemented the plans, encouraging a top-down approach to sustainable development in Europe.
